chapter: Bud Scott band instrumentation and repertoire
title: His role as rhythm guitarist supporting Bud
summary: He was no reader but a loud full-chord guitarist whose heavy wrist and harmony supported Bud's voice.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I'm more than great. I think I know a couple of boys, they just practically done. They retired now, has little jobs, but they're pretty bright after all. They, they pick up one, you know, sometime, in different places, and, you know, do lots of... They've got pretty good voices, and they memorize pretty good, too. You know, I'm pretty good about a whole lot of things they say. They don't have to read or anything, just so long as they've got the talent. I understand they've got the talent. I said, well, I never, just myself, that, uh, you know, I never was much of a reader myself. But, uh, they gave me credit for being about one of these. Whenever I, you showed me something, I made it, and then I could thunder with one of them. I didn't just... They could just hear me above them all, you know. And I learned how to call, just full calls, well, my, some flats, sharps, and so forth. Well, I got those, too, and everything like that. But it seemed like to me that they would always want me... I had to get a heavy wrist. And, uh, with full calls, gave plenty of harmony. That's what Bud liked, because you had to give it behind him. Maybe then he'd drown you out with his voice.
